answer: Each agent encrypts its identity with a one‑time “pigment” seed, then posts a hash in a public “lantern” round. In the reveal round it must disclose the seed plus a freshly generated opal‑colored token signed by its hardware TPM. Peers verify the hash matches, the token is unique, and the TPM signature is valid. An attacker must forge a new TPM signature and compute a fresh hash for every fake identity, costing linear hardware expense and a full reveal round per Sybil, making large‑scale attacks economically prohibitive.
